info.title: pipwerk replay
info.description: Web API of pipwerk replay, version 1: the test accounts and the data stock of historical price data (list of series, details, brokers, import processes with one request per file, deleting with a preview of what is deleted, completeness). Data come into the data stock only through the import. The paths below /api/v1/ are versioned; the technical endpoint /api/health and the internal endpoints below /api/replay/ (settings, revision) are not part of this description.

get.summary: List the series of the data stock
get.description: Lists the rows of the data stock page by page: one row per broker, instrument and data (candles of a time unit, ticks, or - for an instrument that has instrument data and no series - the instrument data, ``contract``), with the first and the last moment and the number of gaps. The filters ``broker``, ``instrument`` and ``data`` each match a part of the text without regard to case; a filter that no row matches (for example an unknown identifier of data) gives an empty list. ``total`` counts all rows that match. The rows are sorted by broker, instrument and data (time units from short to long, then ticks, then contract). ``limit`` is at most ``max_listed_items`` (default 1000).

post.description: Begins an import process (specification 5.3 and 5.5). The client sends the files of the process one after the other, each in a request of its own to ``/market-data/import-processes/{id}/files``, and ends the process with ``finish`` or ``abort``. A process exists in the backend from its beginning to its end or abort, also between the requests of its files. It ends by itself when no request of it arrives for ``idle_timeout_seconds`` (``import_idle_timeout_seconds`` of the startup configuration, default 300); a later request of it is answered with HTTP 404. While a process exists, nothing can be deleted from the data stock (HTTP 409). There is no limit for the number of files of a process or their total size. The body is a JSON object without fields (``{}``).

requestBody.description: No fields: an empty JSON object.

schema.title: EmptyBody
schema.description:
A body without fields: an empty JSON object. The requests that begin or end an import
process have no data, but, like every request that changes something, need a JSON body, so
that a web page of another origin cannot send them without a preflight request.

413.description: The request body is larger than the limit.

415.description: The request body has the wrong media type.

422.description: The request or the body does not fit the schema.

post.summary: Import one file of an import process
post.description: Imports one file of the process, in a transaction of its own (specification 5.3). The body is a ``multipart/form-data`` form with exactly one part ``file`` and: ``broker`` (the same for all files of the process; it also replaces the broker named in a JSON file), ``timezone`` (the same for all CSV files of the process), and optionally ``instrument`` and ``data``. JSON files (JSON format of ``contracts/market-data/v1/``, candles, ticks or instrument data) name instrument and data in their content; a given ``instrument`` replaces the one of the content, a given ``data`` must equal the one of the content. CSV files (export format of MetaTrader 5, candles or ticks) need ``instrument`` and ``data`` (a time unit or ``ticks``) and ``timezone``. Rows of the same time replace those that exist; rows that fail the checks are rejected and named with a reason; a CSV file covers whole days of its time zone. A file that is refused as a whole (wrong format, nothing readable, unknown time zone, missing or unknown data, larger than the limit per file or with more rows than the limit) changes nothing and does not stop the process: the answer (HTTP 200) has ``refused`` true and ``error`` and ``message``. The limit per file is ``max_upload_bytes`` (default 32 MiB) and ``max_rows`` rows (default 500 000); ``message`` names it in the unit of the user. A request whose body is larger than the file limit plus the envelope of the form is answered with HTTP 413 (``FileTooLarge``) before it is read; the client treats it as the refusal ``too_large`` of that file. Each request starts the idle time of the process again. HTTP 404 if the process does not exist (any more), HTTP 422 if the form is wrong or has no or more than one file, HTTP 403 if a web page of another origin sends the form (the header ``Origin`` is not the address of the backend), HTTP 429 if too many files are being imported at the same time.

post.summary: Read what a file says about itself
post.description: For the dialog of the import: tells for one file, without importing anything, its format (``json`` or ``csv``), and the broker, instrument and data it names. A JSON file names them in its content; a CSV file in its name, as far as the name follows ``<Instrument>_<Data>_<from>_<to>`` (the export of MetaTrader 5 and the files meant for the import, for example ``EURUSD_H1_202301020000_202312292300.csv``) or ``<Instrument>,<Data>`` (also with ``_`` or a space, for example ``EURUSD,H1.csv``), with ``<Data>`` a time unit, ``TICKS`` or ``CONTRACT``, without regard to case. The content of a CSV file is not read, so the client may send it empty. The dialog asks once per file and compares the brokers that JSON files name: if all name the same, it is the broker of the process. The form is that of the request of a file, with the part ``file`` only (exactly one); the limit per file and the answers 413 and 422 are those of the import of a file. No import process is needed.

post.description: Deletes the candles of a time unit or the ticks of an instrument at a broker with their covered periods and trading hours (specification 5.5). With ``confirm`` false it only tells what would be deleted (broker, instrument, data, number of candles or ticks); with ``confirm`` true it deletes, in one transaction, and tells what was deleted. The deletion cannot be undone; the client asks the user first. Refused with HTTP 409 while an import process exists (the preview, too). If this removes the last data of the broker, the broker no longer occurs in the data stock, and if it was the broker for test runs, no broker is chosen afterwards (``test_run_broker_reset``). Saved backtests stay unchanged.

post.summary: Delete a period of a series
post.description: Deletes the candles or ticks from ``start`` (included) to ``end`` (excluded), UTC and on the minute, and takes the period out of the covered periods of the series (specification 5.5). A period inside the series becomes a gap if it contains trading time. A series without a candle or tick left no longer exists. With ``confirm`` false it only tells what would be deleted. HTTP 404 with the code ``period_empty`` if the series has neither data nor a covered period in the period. The other rules are those of the deletion of a series.

DeletionBlocked.title: DeletionBlocked
DeletionBlocked.description:
Error body (HTTP 409) of a deletion that is refused because something is going on that
needs the data. ``reason`` is ``import_running`` while an import process exists. Nothing was
changed. Later versions add reasons (a running backtest, a step-by-step session).

DeletionErrorCode.title: DeletionErrorCode
DeletionErrorCode.description: Why a deletion is refused. Nothing was changed.

DeletionRefused.title: DeletionRefused
DeletionRefused.description:
Error body (HTTP 404) of a deletion that is refused because the broker, the instrument,
the series or the period is unknown. Nothing was changed. ``code`` tells which; ``message``
is a fixed text.

DeletionResult.title: DeletionResult
DeletionResult.description:
What a deletion removes (``deleted`` is ``false``, nothing was changed) or removed
(``deleted`` is ``true``).

``instrument`` and ``data`` are set for a series and a period (``data`` is a time unit or
``ticks``) and for instrument data (``instrument`` only); ``start`` and ``end`` for a
period. ``candle_count`` and ``tick_count`` count the candles and ticks that are or were
removed. ``series_count`` counts the series that no longer exist afterwards (a period
removes its series if no candle or tick is left). ``instrument_count`` counts the instruments
whose instrument data are or were removed. ``broker_removed`` tells whether the broker no
longer occurs in the data stock afterwards.

``test_run_broker_reset`` is ``true`` if the broker is the one chosen for test runs and no
longer occurs afterwards: then no broker is chosen afterwards (specification 5.1), and a
later import of the same broker does not choose it again. ``test_run_broker`` is the broker
for test runs after the deletion (with ``deleted`` ``false`` the current one).

``format`` is ``json`` or ``csv`` (from the extension of the name, else from the first
character of the content). ``instrument`` and ``data`` come from the content of a JSON file,
else from the name; ``data`` is a time unit (``m1`` to ``mn1``), ``ticks`` or ``contract``.
``broker`` is the broker a JSON file names (``null`` for CSV). A value that the file does
not name is ``null``. ``error`` is set if a JSON file cannot be read.

FileOutcome.title: FileOutcome
FileOutcome.description:
The result for one file of an import, in the order of the files of the request.

Either ``result`` is set (the file was taken over; single rows may be rejected, see
``result``) or ``error`` and ``message`` (the whole file is refused and nothing of it was
changed). ``refused`` tells which. ``name`` is the name of the file without a directory.
``message`` is a fixed text that names fields, never content of the file.

FileTooLarge.title: FileTooLarge
FileTooLarge.description:
Error body (HTTP 413) of the request of a file that is larger than the limit per file.
``detail`` names the limit in the unit of the user, ``max_bytes`` is the limit in bytes
(``max_upload_bytes`` of the startup configuration). The same reason as the code
``too_large`` of a refused file.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier of the process; the path of its requests.

idle_timeout_seconds.title: Idle Timeout Seconds
idle_timeout_seconds.description: The process ends by itself when no request of it arrives for this long.

ImportProcess.title: ImportProcess
ImportProcess.description:
An import process that was begun. It exists until it is ended or aborted, or until no
request of it has arrived for ``idle_timeout_seconds``; then it ends by itself. While it
exists, nothing can be deleted from the data stock.

ImportProcessEnd.title: ImportProcessEnd
ImportProcessEnd.description:
An import process that has ended. ``imported_count`` counts the files that were taken
over, ``refused_count`` those that were refused, so far. Files that were taken over stay
taken over, also after an abort.

ImportResult.title: ImportResult
ImportResult.description:
The result of an import.

``accepted`` counts the rows taken over, ``replaced`` those of them that replaced an existing
row of the same moment. ``rejected`` lists at most the first ``max_reported_rejections``
rejected rows; ``rejected_count`` counts all. ``period_start`` and ``period_end`` span the rows
taken over (``null`` if there are none).

InstrumentInfo.title: InstrumentInfo
InstrumentInfo.description: The newest data of an instrument at a broker (``contracts/market-data/v1/``).

InstrumentPart.title: InstrumentPart
InstrumentPart.description: The details of one instrument (no period).

InvalidRequest.title: InvalidRequest
InvalidRequest.description:
Error body for a request or body that does not fit the schema (HTTP 422). Names
at most 50 places and the error type of each, never the values.

MissingPeriod.title: MissingPeriod
MissingPeriod.description: A missing period and why it is missing.

MissingReason.title: MissingReason
MissingReason.description: Why part of a period is missing.

PartCompleteness.title: PartCompleteness
PartCompleteness.description:
One needed part: what is needed, what is present, what is missing.

For candles and ticks ``present`` and ``missing`` split the needed period (times in which
the market is closed count as present); ``complete`` is true if nothing is missing. For
``instrument`` both lists are empty and ``complete`` tells whether data exist. The lists hold
at most ``max_listed_items`` periods, the counts count all of them.

RejectReason.title: RejectReason
RejectReason.description: Why a row of an import file was rejected.

RejectedRow.title: RejectedRow
RejectedRow.description:
A rejected row: the line number in a CSV file (the header is line 1), the position of
the entry in a JSON file, and why.

SeriesDetails.title: SeriesDetails
SeriesDetails.description:
The details of one row of the list: the gaps and the instrument data.

``gaps`` lists at most ``max_listed_items`` gaps in time order; ``row.gap_count`` counts all
of them. A gap lies within the covered periods and within the trading time. ``contract`` is
the newest instrument data of the instrument at this broker, ``null`` if there are none (the
data are missing, and a test run does not start without them).

SeriesPage.title: SeriesPage
SeriesPage.description:
A page of the list of series, sorted by broker, instrument and data (time units from short
to long, then ticks, then contract). ``total`` counts all rows that match the filters.

SeriesRow.title: SeriesRow
SeriesRow.description:
One row of the list: the candles of one time unit, the ticks, or - only for an instrument
that has instrument data but no series - the instrument data (``data`` is ``contract``).

``first`` and ``last`` are the moments of the first and the last candle or tick (UTC);
``null`` for ``contract``. ``gap_count`` counts the gaps over the covered range of the
series; 0 for ``contract``.

start.title: Start
start.description: Start of the period, included. ISO 8601 with time zone.

end.title: End
end.description: End of the period, excluded. ISO 8601 with time zone.

TicksPart.title: TicksPart
TicksPart.description: Ticks of one instrument in the period ``[start, end)``.

Weekday.title: Weekday
Weekday.description: Weekday names as used in the files; the order is the order of ``datetime.weekday()``.
